text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Irish actor CYRIL CUSACK, who made his film debut at the age of 7, was born in 1731.
French dramatist EUGENE IONESCO, who initiated 'Theatre of the Absurd', was born in 1912.
The creator of CHARLIE BROWN, SNOOPY, LINUS and the entire "Peanuts" cartoon strip, CHARLES SCHULTZ, was born in 1922.

American singer TINA TURNER, who in recent years has had a close affinity with Rugby League in Australia, was born in 1939. She had hits such as "River Deep, Mountain High" with her husband IKE, and then carved out a successful solo career in the 70s and 80s. Other hits include "Nutbush City Limits"(1973), "Let's Stay Together" (1983), "What's Love Got To Do With It" (1984), "Private Dancer" (1984) and "We Don't Need Another Hero" (1985), "The Best" (1989) and "Steamy Windows" (1989).
Founding member of 'Fleetwood Mac' JOHN McVIE was born in 1945. The British bass players career spans the 60s, 70s, 80s and 90s.
British singer with 'Brotherhood of Man' MARTIN LEE was born in 1949.
** EVENTS **
1832 : New York's public transport system started with
the introduction of horse drawn street cars.
1902 : New Zealand's Progressive Party won the general
election for the fifth consecutive time.
1922 : Tutankhamun's tomb was opened by archaelogist
HOWARD CARTER and his sponsor the Earl of Caernavon. They made a hole in the tomb's door and could distinquish the contents by candlelight.
1928 : The first twins born by Ceasarian section in
Britain were delivered in Manchester.
1949 : Indian Members of Parliament approved India's new
constitution as a "sovereign democratic republic". Two months later India was proclaimed a republic.
1953 : In London, Peers approved the Government's plans
for commercial television.
1956 : Australian sprinter BETTY CUTHBERT won a gold
medal at the Melbourne Olympics for the 100 metres.
1959 : National Service was abolished in Australia.

Defence Minister ATHOL TOWNLEY announced the compulsory service would end from January 1st 1960. More than 200,000 young men had received military training under the scheme which was introduced in 1951. Compulsory military training was first introduced in Australian in 1911 with a scheme for all boys over 12 to take part in school cadet corps training.
1963 : In the biggest one-day rally on Wall Street, share
values rose by 15 billion dollars.
1968 : Rock idol group 'Cream' played their last concert.

Billed as the world's loudest, fastest and most overpowering rock band, the group consisted of ERIC CLAPTON on lead guitar, JACK BRUCE on bass and GINGER BAKER on drums. Their hits included "Strange Brew", "I Feel Free" and "Sunshine of Your Love". The final concert was before 10,000 fans at London's Albert Hall.
1971 : In Melbourne crowds jammed the inner-city streets
for the debut of late-night Friday shopping.
1978 : In New Zealand the Muldoon Government was returned
with a reduced majority.
1983 : An efficient gang of thieves pulled off Britain's

biggest ever robbery. The daring robbers stole more than 46 million dollars worth of gold bullion from a security warehouse at Heathrow airport. They neutralised the alarm system and tied up six guards and then spent an hour coolly loading the gold into a truck.
1987 : Sir JOH BJELKE-PETERSEN was replaced as leader of

Queensland's ruling National Party. Sir JOH has refused to resign as premier but has been replaced as Party leader by MIKE AHERN. A number of Sir JOH's former Ministerial allies were unable to convince him to resign. The final concert was before 10,000 fans at London's Albert Hall.
1990 : President LEE KUAN YEW of Singapore resigned after
26 years in office.
1994 : The last Australian troops returned home after
assisting the United Nations relief operation in Somalia.
